_ramp_comment: S12 (owner, 2026-09-16): `ramp_seconds` is how long the phase schedule below takes to run from its first band to its last, on Normal; a difficulty divides it by `timeline_pace` (36 s on fast, 30 s on super fast) exactly as it divides the run length. It is NOT the run: `run_duration` still keys the boss (95 % of 600 s), so the mix reaches its endgame composition about three quarters of a minute in while the boss still arrives at 9:30. The two used to be one number, which is why compressing the ramp used to drag the boss with it. `interval` below is lerped on the same ramp fraction.
_elite_comment: S12 (owner, 2026-09-16): the opening band is floored at 25 % and every later band carries +15 points over what it used to (0 / 2 / 5 / 10 / 14). Elites are a first-minute enemy now, not a late-run one.
_unused_comment: Enemies benched from the run (owner, 2026-09-17). An id listed here keeps its block in `enemies.json`, its art, its rig, its weights in the bands below and every reference the code and the tests make to it -- it is *disabled*, not deleted. `SpawnTables` drops it from the phase types and the group followers when it reads them, so the director can never roll it; `spawn_at`, `spawn_group` and the dev menu can still seat one deliberately. Re-enabling is deleting a string from this list. Being absent from every band is NOT the same thing: Bonepicker, Gaffjaw and the Hammer Gnome are built and waiting for a band weight, which is pending work rather than a decision to bench them.

placement._band_comment: Placement is a distance band around the hero, regardless of the camera (owner, 2026-09-15): the same request lands the same way at 16:9, 21:9, or with the view anywhere. The strict rung (FAR) takes a point between `far_min_distance` and `far_max_distance` from the hero -- 700 sits just past the 16:9 half-diagonal of 612 world px plus the old 96 px pad, so a 16:9 player still sees nothing appear, while a wider view may see an arrival at its edge; 1100 keeps the walk short. The middle rung (NEAR: a pack whose debt has aged past `relax_after`, or the strict rung empty) drops the ceiling and keeps `near_min_distance` as the keep-away.
placement._starved_comment: The last rung of the relaxation ladder, used only when no point passes the stricter rules -- which is what a player who camps on one island produces: its handful of points are all either on cooldown or inside the keep-away, and every pack becomes debt. At this rung the point cooldown shortens, so the same few points can be reused, and `starved_min_distance` is the only keep-away, so an enemy arrives at the edge of the screen rather than in the hero's lap; candidates here are also weighted by distance, which biases the draw outward.
